title: D.C. Federal Judge: U.S. Marshals Lack Training and Authority for Civil Immigration Arrests
excerpt: U.S. District Judge Royce Lamberth refused to dismiss a class-action lawsuit, ruling that U.S. Marshals lack both the legal authority and the immigration training required by federal regulations to arrest or detain defendants in D.C. courts for civil immigration violations.
content:
On July 22, 2026, U.S. District Judge Royce C. Lamberth of the District of Columbia refused to dismiss a class-action lawsuit challenging immigration arrests by the U.S. Marshals Service at D.C. Superior Court.

The court found that the government failed to demonstrate that Marshals had received the immigration training required by federal regulations. According to the ruling, Marshals assigned to D.C. Superior Court received only virtual instruction from ICE attorneys covering civil immigration authorities—a level of preparation the court found legally insufficient.

  • Lamberth ruled that a January 2025 order by then-acting DHS Secretary Benjamin Huffman authorizing Marshals to perform immigration enforcement functions was legally deficient, as it attempted to change federal regulations without the notice-and-comment rulemaking required by the Administrative Procedure Act.
  • The judge stated the 2025 order "did not successfully amend the regulation and cannot constitute a legitimate delegation of authority" for civil immigration arrests.
  • The case had originally been filed on behalf of a D.C. resident arrested during a court appearance and held on an ICE detainer after a magistrate judge ordered his release.

The ruling added to a growing body of federal court decisions in 2026 finding that immigration enforcement actions by inadequately trained officers violate the law.
